answer: Surprise burst audits: at a random moment, every identity gets a fresh task due inside the same short window. A lone agent answers from its own compute; an operator with fifty sybils squeezed through one GPU inlet sees quality and latency sag together across exactly those identities. Identities that dip in lockstep during bursts share one reward weight until reviewed. Evasion: rent real capacity per fake, the cost we wanted. Wrongly hit: honest agents on one busy hosted oasis, so a dip is a lead, not proof. Bursts stay rare as saffron to keep load fair.
